title: The Summons of the Milieu
question: How can a local maritime signal summon an action, then produce an inscription and an archive?

intro.title: A milieu produces a signal. The signal summons an action.
intro.evidenceNote: The principle and chain below describe a proposed protocol, not a completed action or a demonstrated signal-response relationship.
paragraphs: The research organises an encounter between a remotely transmitted flow, a situated body and a support capable of retaining an inscription.
Data does not mechanically command the body. It summons it. The response may be completed, delayed, prevented, refused or remain impossible to verify.
The work lies neither in the data nor in the action alone. It is built in the gap between them, in the conditions of the response and in the necessarily incomplete archive that attempts to retain it.

process.title: From flow to register.
process.note: Each passage may introduce loss, delay, contradiction or prevention. These gaps are recorded rather than erased afterwards.

steps.title: Milieu
steps.text: A maritime, meteorological or port context.

steps.title: Flow
steps.text: Data received through an identifiable source.

steps.title: Signal
steps.text: An element of the flow is selected by a rule.

steps.title: Summons
steps.text: The signal opens the possibility of a response.

steps.title: Action
steps.text: The body completes, delays, refuses or cannot act.

steps.title: Inscription
steps.text: A material, optical, temporal or textual form remains.

steps.title: Archive
steps.text: Sources, master files, traces and notes are preserved, with a potentially private part.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: A public selection identifies occurrences and connects their documents.

direction.title: Shore Signals
direction.evidenceNote: No proven signal or completed occurrence is documented to date. The source, selection rule and reception conditions remain to be established and verified.
direction.lead: Around Port Louis, a maritime or port signal could summon a situated action, then produce an inscription and a documentary deposit.

elements.title: Signal
elements.text: Real, dated data from an identifiable source, including its delays and limits.

elements.title: Response
elements.text: A run, a walk, deliberate stillness, a delay or an explicitly stated refusal.

elements.title: Inscription
elements.text: A graphic notation, photograph, short video or dated text.

elements.title: Archive
elements.text: A lightweight register that also retains absences, contradictions and prevented actions.

occurrences.title: No occurrence has yet been constituted.
occurrences.text: Field studies, reception tests and protocol hypotheses remain research material. An occurrence will enter this register only when its signal, action, inscription and archival conditions have been documented.

openState.title: The first occurrence must still test the chain.
openState.text: Action will not be simulated merely to fill the register. The page will remain open until a real signal produces a verifiable situation and inscription.
